pr_title: Add expiration of unused refresh tokens
pr_body:

## Breaking change
<!--

  This piece of text is published with the release notes, so it helps if you
  write it towards our users, not us.
  Note: Remove this section if this PR is NOT a breaking change.
-->
Refresh tokens will be automatically deleted when unused. A refresh token is considered unused if it has not been used for a login within 90 days.
If you need a permanent token, then we recommend using [Long-lived access tokens](https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/auth_api/#long-lived-access-token).

This adds an expiration period for unused refresh tokens of 90 days.
This only applies for "normal" (_`TOKEN_TYPE_NORMAL`_) tokens.

> New refresh tokens will be automatically deleted when unused. A refresh token is considered unused if it has not been used for a login within 90 days. This only applies to newly created refresh tokens (i.e. for new login sessions).

I discussed this yesterday with some and I want to change this to apply to existing refresh tokens too. Let me add a little context.

Initially, this was discussed on Discord, where the concern was raised: We don't know how existing refresh tokens are used: maybe in some applications... This resulted in the idea of only using it for new tokens.

However, there is no normal way to create these tokens manually. Any token you've created in the UI for these purposes (e.g., to hook up Node-RED or anything else) are long-lived access tokens (to which this logic already doesn't apply).

What is left is potentially a logged-in user, that hasn't used their application in 3 months or more. In the, assumingly, rare case that happens, a user will be logged out and can log in again.

The latter is the intended behavior of this change anyways.

../Frenck

I agree. The majority of these tokens are never going to get cleaned up if we don't start the 3 month timer on all the old ones as well.  If we wanted to be extra safe we could set the timer to be 6mo or 1yr for the old ones to give people time to sort things out if they only have access to HA one a year because they have the install in a remote location... but that seems like an extreme case.

I'm also fine with let exiting tokens expire, too👍 
We can also set the initial expiration to 180 or 360 days, but they would shorten to 90 days as soon as these token were used. if we want keep these increased expiration period for "old" tokens, we need to do some extra checks based on the `version` property of the `RefreshToken`, but i'm not sure if this it worth to do 🤔 
I'm happy to follow any advice on this and adjust the PR accordingly 😊
Let's do 90 days for all.

issue_context.title: Pile up of useless abandoned refresh tokens in user profile
issue_context.body:
### The problem

I have hundreds of old "refresh tokens" in my user profile (see screenshot). I guess they stem from sessions that where not ended by "logout" button but by closing the browser.
Since those tokens are useless and are against privacy because you can see when user logged in, what I do not need, I want now to mass delete those month old tokens.

There should be a configurable threshold for auto-deleting those tokens, e.g. 1 month.
See also this thread where people programmed scripts to mass delete those tokens.
https://community.home-assistant.io/t/delete-old-abandoned-refresh-tokens-from-user-profiles/126823

![screenshot](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/assets/131813959/18dc3ea6-a078-4202-ac8f-8774ba1cb7bb)

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

comments:
I am suffering of thousands of tokens myself. 

In addition to being a privacy issue it is a GUI issue since the huge list makes using the webpage hard to use (lot of scrolling on a mobile device to get past the token list).

I think this clean-up should be done scheduled every now and then. The active tokens (last used in X days) would be kept and long-lived access tokens as well of course.

Someone even made an add-on to clean these tokens up. The problem is, the scripts and the add-on all need a restart of Home Assistant, since the tokens are kept in memory and will not get removed unless Home Assistant is stopped. So the currently available fixes for this problem depend on constant reboots.
Keeping unused tokens is potentially a security issue. I would like to see them automatically cleaned up

@mib1185 As a software developer by trade and hobby, I understand why you would have flagged this as a Feature Request. As a user, I must stress the criticality of this "Feature" — a lack of it brings out the enormous amount of pain in the User's profile page, causing it to freeze for minutes (and on some client devices that freeze causes a whole system crash).

Essentially, devices that login through `trusted_networks` with `allow_bypass_login` set to `true` seems to create a new refresh token every time that device displays any page in Home Assistant.

Some of these devices can be Google Cast targets (e.g. Nest Hub Displays) and periodically have to be refreshed. That refresh causes a new token to be issued. From only a year's worth of these dashboards being cast periodically, my auth file is now **6.5MB**. 🤯

Please, prioritize this feature as a component to fixing a huge technical debt in authentication.

Much appreciated.

The downside is that `last_used_at` and `created_at` are doing datetime objects

For this case I think timestamps are a better fit

I try to use datetime for these cases:
- displaying to humans
- when I care about doing something on Wednesdays
- a specific, hour/minute

I try to use timestamps for these case:
- durations
- comparing/firing at a specific points in time

i've applied your suggestion and reworked it to use timestamps instead of datetimes ->
 [use timestamp for expire_at bf04edf](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/108428/commits/bf04edf9b54df0475c0b7bd9052d5b321954f5d7)
